subject: Decision grid & delegation — annual targets and scenario decisioning
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Decision grid & delegation — annual targets and scenario decisioning

Team —

As we move into the annual targets window, I want to propose a lightweight decision grid for who signs off on which levers and what threshold triggers escalation to Exec. Objective is to keep the OKR/target process fast while making handoffs and accountability explicit.

Attached: decision-grid-v1.xlsx (single-sheet grid) and timeline-and-decision-calendar.pdf (proposed review dates).

High-level asks:
- Please review the grid and add an owner for each row column by EOD Tuesday 6/22.
- Call out any gate thresholds that are unrealistic for your org (we'll iterate).
- Marcus: can you own the financial modeling cell (cost/ARR sensitivity)?
- Hannah: please confirm the OKR alignment column maps to your QBR cadence.

Proposed timeline (short):
- 6/22: internal alignment on owners and gates
- 6/29: preliminary targets submitted to Finance
- 7/06: leadership review and finalization

I want this to be pragmatic: three scenarios (base, downside 15%, downside 30%) with clear decision rules for when we default to the downside playbook and who approves reforecasting vs. hiring freezes.

Thanks — will gather inputs and push a cleaned grid back into the shared sheet.

Marissa Cole
VP, GTM Strategy and Ops
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: decision-grid-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB), timeline-and-decision-calendar.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision grid & delegation — annual targets and scenario decisioning

+1 on the approach — thanks Marissa. A couple quick notes:
- Add a column for "pricing sensitivity" tied to unit economics. I think we need that explicitly since small pricing changes materially change ARR/GM for targeted products.
- Suggest Aditya take the lead on the pricing sensitivity row and coordinate with Marcus on model inputs.

If folks are comfortable I'll add a Pricing row to the grid and a short note on assumptions.

Vivek
Chief Product Officer

Date: 2027-06-19T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Decision grid & delegation — annual targets and scenario decisioning

Marissa —

This looks good and pragmatic. A few governance points from Finance:
- We need explicit gating thresholds for any hiring delta > 10% FTE in a function or > $500K incremental run-rate.
- Any scenario that changes ARR by more than 8% needs a CFO-level sign-off prior to rollout.
- Marcus: please prepare a one-page summary of model input ranges for Finance to consume (cost buckets + revenue sensitivity).

Looping in Finance Ops (cc'd) to confirm they can meet the 6/29 timeline for preliminary targets.

I'll also attach a short doc with budget gate criteria to help standardize decisions.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance & Operations
Redwood Inference

Thank you — great notes. Summary / next steps: 
- Marcus to deliver the one-page model input ranges to Finance by Tue 6/22 EOD (owner: Marcus Lin).
- Aditya to populate pricing sensitivity assumptions in the shared sheet by Mon 6/21 (owner: Aditya Rao).
- All leaders to add owners to the decision grid by Tue 6/22 EOD.
- Quick alignment meeting: Tue 6/22 10:30–11:00am PT (30m) — calendar invite to follow.
- Finance Ops to confirm 6/29 preliminary target intake window; Laura will track.

I'll consolidate the inputs into the Google sheet (link below) after the meeting and push a versioned grid into HubSpot (HS-2198) for tracking. Please flag any blockers asap.
